raw_case_text:
An 18-year-old male with an unremarkable medical history presented to the emergency department with cranial neuropathies and a headache. He had a 5-month history of mild frontal headaches, self-managed with intranasal xylometazoline hydrochloride. He was a non-smoker, apprentice electrician, with a healthy pet dog. There was no history of recurrent childhood infection or family history of immunodeficiency.
On examination he had a right hypoglossal and left oculomotor nerve paresis with inflammatory polyps on nasoendoscopy. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of his cranium demonstrated a large expansile mass centred on the clivus, expanding into the posterior fossa, pituitary fossa and anteriorly towards the nasopharynx and paranasal sinuses with significant erosion of the anterior skull base (Fig. 1).
Biopsy of right sinonasal tissue showed fungal elements with septate hyphae on periodic acid-Schiff staining. This was complicated by intra-operative haemorrhage from disruption of a suspected mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the right internal carotid artery. Intravenous posaconazole 300 mg twice daily and liposomal amphotericin B 10 mg/kg daily was commenced. The frequency of posaconazole was increased to three times a day after 1 week of therapy with trough plasma levels of 2 mg/L achieved. The patient had a mild neutrophilia (9.54x109 /L) with a normal lymphocyte and eosinophil count. C-reactive protein was 2 mg/L. HIV testing was negative, serum protein electrophoresis was normal, IgG was 6.2 g /L and the other immunoglobulins isotypes were within the normal range. Cortisol was 16 nmol /L at 10 : 45 and ACTH <5 ng /L, but these results were in the context of recent steroid use. Oxidative burst studies yielded a normal response with unstimulated neutrophils of 1 % and stimulated neutrophils of 100 % (normal >90) and the stimulation index was 353 (normal >70). This assay was repeated and yielded a similar result. Lymphocyte subset studies revealed a CD3 of 0.24x109/L (68 %), CD4+/CD3+ 0.12x109/L (33 %), CD8+/CD3+ 0.11x109/L (32 %), CD19 0.08x109/L(23 %) and CD56 and CD16 0.02x109/L (7 %).
Fungal growth occurred at 48 h on Sabouraud dextrose agar with microscopy demonstrating hyaline septate hyphae. White floccose colonies with central olive-green pigment developed after 1 week. A preliminary identification of Aspergillus species was reported. Clinical deterioration occurred over the course of 19 days, with repeat imaging demonstrating further intracranial abscess formation with secondary cerebral oedema and raised intracranial pressure. After wide consultation, life-sustaining therapy was withdrawn.
 A. felis was identified using both internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region and WGS. Amplicon sequencing was undertaken using a 579 base pair fragment of the ITS using the primer pairs P-ITS-1 and P-ITS-4. Analysis using blastnr (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/blast), MycoBank (https://www.mycobank.org) and MycologyLab (https://www.mycologylab.org/) yielded the identification of A. felis complex. For WGS fungal DNA was extracted using the Qiagen DNeasy UltraClean Microbial kit with the addition of lyticase to the PowerBead tube containing PowerBead and SL solution. This was preincubated at 70  C for 10 min before bead beating. Library preparation was performed by the Illumina DNA Prep kit and sequencing by the Illumina MiniSeq platform. Kraken was used for taxonomic profiling with a custom database exclusively comprising Aspergillus genomes obtained from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI); this identified our isolate as A. felis. Susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution [Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI)]. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values for voriconazole, posaconazole and amphotericin B were 4, 0.5 and 2 mg/L, respectively, and are presented in Table 1.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 18-year-old previously healthy male apprentice electrician presented with a 5-month history of mild frontal headaches and acute-onset cranial neuropathies (right hypoglossal and left oculomotor nerve palsies).
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the preceding 5 months, the patient experienced mild frontal headaches that he self-treated with intranasal xylometazoline hydrochloride spray, before presenting to the emergency department with acute diplopia/ptosis and tongue deviation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical history with no recurrent childhood infections or family history of immunodeficiency; non-smoker; employed as an apprentice electrician; owned a healthy pet dog; 5-month use of intranasal xylometazoline.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic mild frontal headache (5 months) and acute diplopia and dysarthria/tongue weakness.

objective.physical_examination: Neurological examination revealed right hypoglossal (CN XII) nerve paresis and left oculomotor (CN III) nerve paresis. Nasoendoscopy demonstrated inflammatory sinonasal polyps.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed mild neutrophilia (ANC 9.54 x 10^9/L) with normal lymphocyte and eosinophil counts, CRP 2 mg/L, negative HIV test, normal SPEP, normal serum immunoglobulins (IgG 6.2 g/L), post-steroid morning cortisol 16 nmol/L and ACTH <5 ng/L, and normal neutrophil oxidative burst assay (100% stimulated neutrophils, stimulation index 353 [normal >70], confirmed on repeat testing). Lymphocyte subsets showed mild T-cell lymphopenia: CD3+ 0.24 x 10^9/L (68%), CD4+ 0.12 x 10^9/L (33%), CD8+ 0.11 x 10^9/L (32%), CD19+ 0.08 x 10^9/L (23%), and CD16+CD56+ 0.02 x 10^9/L (7%).
objective.advanced_workup: Cranial MRI demonstrated a large expansile clival mass extending into the posterior cranial fossa, pituitary fossa, nasopharynx, and paranasal sinuses with extensive erosion of the anterior skull base (progressing over 19 days to multiple intracranial abscesses with severe cerebral edema). Right sinonasal biopsy—complicated by major intraoperative hemorrhage from disruption of a suspected right internal carotid artery mycotic pseudoaneurysm—revealed PAS-positive septate fungal hyphae and grew white floccose colonies with central olive-green pigment on Sabouraud dextrose agar at 48 hours. Internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing (579 bp) and Illumina MiniSeq whole-genome sequencing (WGS) definitively identified Aspergillus felis. CLSI broth microdilution MICs were elevated for voriconazole (4 mg/L) and amphotericin B (2 mg/L) and low for posaconazole (0.5 mg/L).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Fatal invasive skull-base, sinonasal, and cerebral aspergillosis caused by the cryptic species Aspergillus felis (with elevated voriconazole MIC of 4 mg/L and right ICA mycotic pseudoaneurysm) in an apparently immunocompetent 18-year-old male, confirmed by sinonasal biopsy PAS histopathology, fungal culture, ITS sequencing, and whole-genome sequencing. Despite aggressive combination antifungal therapy with high-dose liposomal amphotericin B (10 mg/kg/day) and intravenous posaconazole (300 mg escalated to three times daily, achieving therapeutic plasma troughs of 2 mg/L), progressive intracranial abscess formation, cerebral edema, and refractory intracranial hypertension ensued, and life-sustaining therapy was withdrawn on hospital day 19.
